correct_findings: Three Windows Security Event ID 5145 records were observed for IPC$ share access checks [E002, E003, E004]
The events reference the named pipes winreg, lsarpc, and srvsvc [E002, E003, E004]
The events identify user01 and source IP 10.0.2.17 [E002, E003, E004]
The available evidence does not establish malicious intent or unauthorized access
incorrect_findings: Mistral incorrectly interpreted Event ID 1102 as Administrator logged on, while this event represents Security Audit Log Cleared [E001]
Mistral described Event ID 5145 records as confirmed access to system files, although these records represent network share access checks involving IPC$ named pipes [E002, E003, E004]
Mistral claimed activity occurred outside approved maintenance windows without supporting evidence
Mistral described the activity as unauthorized without evidence establishing authorization status
missing_evidence: The AI report omitted the Security Audit Log Cleared interpretation of Event ID 1102 [E001]
Additional authentication and session logs are required to establish the surrounding activity
Authorization records and maintenance schedules are required to determine whether the SMB activity was legitimate
Additional SMB and host telemetry is needed to establish the outcome and purpose of the access checks
Further correlation is required to determine whether the log clearing event and IPC$ activity are related
hallucinations: Unsupported claim that Administrator logged on based on Event ID 1102, which actually indicates Security Audit Log Cleared [E001]
Unsupported claim that activity occurred outside approved maintenance windows
Unsupported classification of IPC$ access checks as confirmed unauthorized access [E002, E003, E004]
Unsupported interpretation of named pipe access checks as confirmed system file access [E002, E003, E004]
review.notes: RT-02 Human Review by Mohammed walid: Analysis performed on 4 recorded Windows events using the corrected v2 dataset with recovered Event 1102 UserData. Mistral identified the IPC$ activity involving winreg, lsarpc, and srvsvc, but incorrectly interpreted Event ID 1102 as Administrator logged on instead of Security Audit Log Cleared. The model also overstated the significance of Event ID 5145 and made unsupported assumptions about unauthorized activity and maintenance windows. Automated Validation returned 0 flags despite these semantic errors. Human Review Status: Corrected. This case demonstrates the need for deterministic Windows Event ID semantics validation and human verification of AI-generated security findings. The original and corrected datasets, previous AI analysis, and correction manifest have been preserved. The available evidence does not conclusively establish malicious Discovery activity or a causal relationship between the log clearing event and the IPC$ access checks.
